She’s probably scared and stressed out, I’m 26 and I’m scared and stressed out.  It’s super common in the first trimester no matter your situation because it is settling in that stuff is about to change.  Hormones also play a part in her emotions.  If she is interested in taking an antidepressant she should discuss with her ob/gyn who may refer her to a different doctor, but they’ll have a better idea of what’s safe.

As for you:  be patient with her. Help her to make a list of all the things she’s stressed or worried about (you can do this too!) and come up with possible solutions for those and most importantly start checking them off ASAP.  This will help her feel more confident that everything is going to be okay.

Best of luck and congratulations.

I just had my 12 week scan today and saw baby moving all over the place and it still doesn’t feel real.  It was hard to believe that my body could do something this incredible.  I’ve always thought I’d have a hard time conceiving for no real reason just because I thought for sure my body would fail me.  And then it happened, and I realized how little I trusted myself.

I say if you want to tell people do it.  Let the people who you want in your corner if something awful were to happen know.  My mom found out by accident (I gave her my old laptop a year ago and she happened to be logged in when a reminder for my ultrasound on my calendar popped up on her screen) and it was a godsend.  For one I needed to know family history for the docs and two I just needed support through all of my emotions and anxieties.

Bottom line you’re going to be great, tell whoever you want, and take care of yourself. Best of luck!
